doc.title: International databases — search syntax and access
doc.markdown:
# International databases — search syntax and access
For each database: Boolean syntax, access notes, export format, and execution mode (skill executes directly vs. user executes manually).
Mark each one in the protocol with: - **Direct:** skill executes via API/scraping - **Guided:** skill provides string + instructions; user executes - **Hybrid:** skill executes a partial query; user fills gaps
## arXiv (Direct)
- API: https://export.arxiv.org/api/query - Free, no auth. - Boolean: `cat:cs.AI AND (abs:transformer AND abs:"time series")`. Fields: `ti`, `au`, `abs`, `co`, `jr`, `cat`, `id`, `all`. - Date range: `submittedDate:[202001010000 TO 202612312359]`. - Returns Atom feed; parse with `feedparser`. - Use `scripts/search_arxiv.py`.
## Semantic Scholar (Direct)
- API: https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search - Free; rate-limited (100 req / 5 min unauthenticated, higher with API key). - Query is plain text (no Boolean operators in v1; use `&fieldsOfStudy=`, `&year=`, `&publicationTypes=` for filtering). - Returns JSON with paperId, title, abstract, authors, year, venue, citationCount, references, openAccessPdf. - Use `scripts/search_semantic_scholar.py`.
## dblp (Direct)
- API: https://dblp.org/search/publ/api?q=...&format=json - Free, no auth, fast. Best for completeness in CS. - Query syntax: `term1 term2$ year:2020:2026 type:Conference_and_Workshop_Papers|Journal_Articles` (terms with `$` are exact). Boolean is implicit AND; use `|` for OR. - Returns JSON. No abstracts (dblp is bibliographic only) — pair with Semantic Scholar to enrich. - Use `scripts/search_dblp.py`.
## Crossref (Direct)
- API: https://api.crossref.org/works?query=... - Free, no auth. - Filters: `&filter=from-pub-date:2020,until-pub-date:2026,type:journal-article`. - Useful for DOI resolution and bibliographic completeness; abstracts often missing.
## Google Scholar (Guided)
- No official API. Programmatic scraping is rate-limited and ToS-sensitive. - Skill approach: `web_search` with query like `site:scholar.google.com "exact phrase" topic` — but results are limited. - Better approach: instruct user to use Scholar manually with the booleans, export to BibTeX (using "Cite" → "BibTeX"), and paste back. Up to ~1000 results per query (Scholar caps). - Boolean syntax in Scholar: standard, with `OR` (must be uppercase), `-` to exclude, `"phrase"` for exact, `intitle:`, `author:`, `source:` operators.
## ACM Digital Library (Hybrid)
- https://dl.acm.org/ - Some content is OA (especially since the ACM OA initiative); the rest is paywalled. - Boolean syntax (Advanced Search): `[All: transformer] AND [All: "time series"] AND [Publication Date: (01/01/2020 TO 12/31/2026)]`. - Export: BibTeX or RIS via "Export Citations". - Skill: `web_search` for OA portion, instruct user for the rest.
## IEEE Xplore (Guided unless institutional access)
- https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/ - Mostly paywalled. Institutional access via IP or proxy. - Boolean syntax: `(("Document Title":transformer) AND ("All Metadata":"time series"))`. - Filters: Year range, Publication Type, IEEE journals/conferences. - Export: CSV (top 100), BibTeX (top 25), or "Save This Search" for persistence. - Skill: provide string + instructions; if user has institutional access, optionally generate a Python script using their library proxy URL. Never bypass the paywall.
## Scopus (Guided)
- https://www.scopus.com/ - Paywalled; nearly always institutional. - Boolean syntax: `TITLE-ABS-KEY ( transformer AND "time series" ) AND PUBYEAR > 2019 AND PUBYEAR < 2027 AND DOCTYPE ( ar OR cp )`. - Operators: `AND, OR, AND NOT, W/n` (within n words), `PRE/n` (X precedes Y by n). - Export: CSV or BibTeX, up to 2000 records per export. - Scopus has its own API (Elsevier Developer) but requires API key + institutional subscription.
## Web of Science / Clarivate (Guided)
- https://www.webofscience.com/ - Paywalled, institutional. - Boolean syntax: `TS=(transformer AND "time series") AND PY=(2020-2026) AND DT=(Article OR Proceedings Paper)`. Field tags: `TS=topic, TI=title, AU=author, SO=source, AB=abstract`. - Export: tab-delimited or BibTeX, up to 1000 records. - WoS Lite API exists but is institutional.
## ScienceDirect / Elsevier (Guided)
- https://www.sciencedirect.com/ - Paywalled, institutional. - Search syntax: simpler — uses field selectors in advanced search UI. - Has OA content that's freely accessible. - Elsevier ScienceDirect API for institutional users.
## Springer Link (Guided)
- https://link.springer.com/ - Mix of OA and paywalled. - Search syntax: standard Boolean with field qualifiers in advanced search. - Springer API: free with key, https://dev.springernature.com/.
## Unpaywall (Direct, helper)
- API: https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/{DOI}?email=... - Free, requires email parameter. Returns whether a paper has an OA copy and the URL. - Use during full-text retrieval phase to find legal OA versions of paywalled papers.
## Strategy when user has institutional access
If the user confirms access to Scopus / WoS / IEEE Xplore / ScienceDirect / Springer:
1. Build the proper Boolean string in that base's syntax. 2. Generate a Python script using `requests` + `requests.Session` that authenticates via the institution's proxy (e.g., `https://{base}.{proxy.uni.edu}/`). 3. The script downloads only what the user is entitled to access. 4. Output: CSV of metadata + downloaded PDFs in `pdfs/` folder.
**Never bypass paywalls.** The script is a convenience automating manual access the user already has.
## Strategy when user lacks institutional access
1. Build the Boolean string and document it in the protocol anyway (for reproducibility). 2. Mark the base as "documented but executed manually by user" or "not executed". 3. Recommend the user use other free bases (arXiv, Semantic Scholar, dblp, Crossref) intensively. 4. Suggest snowballing from a high-quality seed paper as a complement.
